feasible.reason: The proposal is sound against the stated threat (post-factory, pre-first-power implant tapping the display SPI or button nets) and is correctly flagged kind=hardware, cost L, P0. Repo facts hold: pq1's NV3007 is write-only with PA6 NC (secure/src/hw/lcd_nv3007.rs:104, fsbl/src/render.rs:62-72), the seed wizard streams the 24 words as pixels over SPI1 (secure/src/ui/seed_wizard.rs:89-96), the EVT board exposes J210 SWD pads, PB8/PB9 I2C1 pads and an SBU-driven BOOT0 (docs/hardware/evt-debug-pins.md, gh #695), and there is no BOM, no enclosure spec and no schematic cross-check (docs/hardware/schematics/README.md, docs/hardware/pcb/README.md). With no readback from the panel, firmware genuinely cannot detect a passive SPI tap, so removing the cavity and the reachable copper is the right class of counter and matches Ledger/Cypherock precedent. The bypasses that exist (factory-side insertion, whole-device substitution, a reflash over the deliberately-kept SWD pads at RDP-0) are either explicitly delegated to IMP-02/IMP-03 or are covered by the verify-before-first-power route, so none refutes it; they do need the corrections below.
feasible.corrections: 1) The rationale overclaims: only the cavity removal is deterministic. "Destructive-open" and the X-ray/weight/photo comparables are detection claims that depend on the user actually inspecting and on the attacker not being able to re-weld or substitute the shell; state it as raising attacker cost/skill, not as threshold-free. 2) "Zero void behind the panel" is narrower than the title's "no-cavity enclosure": the supercap, USB-C, dome-switch actuator and connector regions are unavoidable voids, so the load-bearing requirement is the copper rule, not the void rule. Specify the SPI1/DC/TE/button nets as stripline between two ground planes (the V10 board is already 6-layer), not merely "inner layers": an adjacent-outer-layer capacitive pickup plate over an unshielded inner trace still recovers a few-MHz MOSI stream. 3) Button nets cannot be fully buried (they terminate at mechanical contacts, and sheet 2 shows a button connector); a PA0/PA1 tap leaks the PIN press pattern, not the seed, so rank SPI1/DC isolation above buttons and pot the button and display FPC connectors. 4) Keeping SWD pads reachable for IMP-02 keeps an RDP-0 reflash path open to the same interdictor; the proposal must make the user's pre-first-power SWD verification mandatory (or seal the pads) rather than rely on the enclosure for that window. 5) BOOT0-strap verification on a sealed unit can be done non-destructively from outside (apply the A8<->VBUS bridge, assert no 0483:df11 enumeration) plus one destructive teardown to read R121/R119; note the strap only matters in the pre-RDP-2 window, which is exactly the interdiction window. 6) Cheap, non-deterministic hardware complements exist and should be listed as separate kind=hardware items, not folded in: a sense resistor on the panel/backlight rail read by ADC, and a GPIO RC/capacitance self-test of PA4/PA5/PA7 to catch added load; both are threshold-based and need a per-design baseline. 7) Nothing here can be verified on current units: EVT-003B-class sealed units and the AL_A66_MB_V10 EVT board are not retrofittable, so this is MP-revision-only and ODM-gated; the first repo-side deliverable is the schematic cross-check and BOM that the docs admit are missing, which this proposal depends on but does not list as a prerequisite.

vendor-claim.reason: The vendor_precedent is substantively true and novelty='parity' is correct: Ledger (Nano Gen5 one-piece casing that cannot be opened without visible, irreversible damage), Cypherock (ultrasonic weld as tamper evidence; Keylabs test-point/jig finding), Foundation (debug pads under the display, two active tamper pins that wipe SECURAM on opening) and Coldcard (welded clear case) all demonstrably ship something on this axis, so the proposal is catching up, not leading. The repo evidence checks out line-for-line (write-only panel, no-MISO verdict caveat, 24 words rendered over SPI1, SWD/BOOT0/I2C1 pads documented as 'DNP for MP, pads stay', no BOM, cross-check not done, gh #695 open). The precedent is INCOMPLETE rather than false: it omits Trezor entirely (Model One/T casings are ultrasonically welded; Safe 3/5 are marketed as tamper-evident; Safe 7 firmware ships an external tamper input that erases secrets in production builds), names the implant case 'CryptoBilis' (a name that appears in none of the cited materials; the documented case is Joe Grand's Nano X implant), and misattributes the Parasitic Circus paper (it is PDN-impedance golden-free verification, not X-ray/weight/photos). The donjon URL supports only the Genuine-Check limit, not the casing/photos remedy, which lives in Ledger support article 4404382029329 and in the Grand slides' 'Ledger response' slide.
vendor-claim.corrections:
1) TREZOR PRECEDENT OMITTED. trezor.io 'Trezor hardware: built-in security' states Model One and Model T casings are 'assembled using ultrasonic welding ... no connective bolts, nails, soldering materials, or adhesives', and lists Safe 3 and Safe 5 with 'a tamper evident casing ... designed to reveal physical manipulation attempts' (Safe 7: aluminium unibody, no tamper-evident claim). In trezor-firmware code, Safe 7 (T3W1) defines TAMPER_INPUT_2 (core/embed/models/T3W1/boards/trezor_t3w1_rev{A,B,C}.h:298/308/326); core/embed/sec/tamper/stm32u5/tamper.c:100-176 configures TAMP_IN2 (read on GPIOA pin 0 at :182-197) with 'TAMP->CR3 = 0' = confirmed mode, comment 'all secrets all deleted when any tamper event is triggered'; core/embed/projects/kernel/main.c:139-142 enables it only '#if PRODUCTION'; core/embed/projects/boardloader/main.c:84-85 calls tamper_init(); prodtest exposes 'tamper-read' (core/embed/projects/prodtest/README.md:1200-1207). Nothing in the Trezor tree covers no-cavity/potting/test-pad removal (grep for ultrasonic|potting|tamper-evident|test pad over *.c/*.h/*.rs/*.md returned only two unrelated prodtest lines), so that part of the proposal is a mechanical/ODM matter for Trezor too. Aside: Trezor's ST7789 driver reads back the panel ID (core/embed/io/display/st-7789/display_panel.c:54-93, RDDID 0x04/0xD3) — a display read-back path pq1's no-MISO NV3007 wiring lacks (secure/src/hw/lcd_nv3007.rs:104; fsbl/src/render.rs:62-72).
2) 'CryptoBilis' IS NOT A DOCUMENTED NAME. It appears in none of the five sources nor in web search. The actual case: Joe Grand, 'Reverse Engineering a Ledger Nano X Hardware Implant' (hardwear.io USA 2026 / Tropicon 2026; first contact = Reddit r/ledgerwallet 'Nano X being sold to steal your crypto', Aug 2025). Slides (grandideastudio.com/media/ledger_hardware_implant_slides.pdf, 134 MB, pdftotext): 'Battery has reduced size in order to fit implant'; 'OLED connects to the Nano X Secure Element via SPI'; 'Implant monitors SPI traffic between Nano X Secure Element and OLED ... Template matcher functions look for the glyphs ... Recovery seed ... stored in Flash at 0x7000 ... transmitted via cellular module' (Luat Air700E, 4G LTE, 8 cm coil antenna ~937 MHz); 'New iterations of implant have already been spotted'; 'LEDGER RESPONSE: Check hardware integrity against known-good pictures; Follow best practices when buying ... Ledger is looking into further hardening'. So the threat shape (MCU + LTE on the display SPI) is accurate, but the cavity was the battery bay, not 'padding behind the screen'. Replace 'CryptoBilis shape' with 'Grand 2026 Nano X implant shape'.
3) SOURCE MAPPING. donjon.ledger.com/threat-model/device-genuineness supports only: 'a Genuine check cannot detect unauthorized physical modifications to the hardware, such as spying implants, if the original Secure Element remains intact' and that it 'cannot verify the device's physical supply chain history'; it says NOTHING about casing or PCB photos. The casing claim is in support.ledger.com/article/4404382029329-zd ('Check hardware integrity'): Nano Gen5 one-piece casing is tamper-evident and cannot be opened without visible and irreversible damage; Stax 'isn't built for routine opening'; opening voids warranty (page is JS-rendered — confirmed via search snippets, not a direct fetch). The 'photos' remedy is Ledger's historical 'Check hardware integrity' chapters (Nano S/X manuals) and the Grand slide above. Ledger's 2018 stance 'We have designed the Nano S to be easily openable, so you can check the integrity of the device yourself' (ledger.com post on wallet.fail) is confirmed, so the risks field is right that pq1 would be choosing the Gen5 model over the Nano S model.
4) PARASITIC CIRCUS MISATTRIBUTED. arXiv 2403.12252 (Safa, Schaumont, Tajik) is golden-free PCB verification by Power-Delivery-Network IMPEDANCE characterization, replacing a physical golden board with a simulated signature from design files; it does not propose X-ray, weight or photo comparison. Cite it for a PDN-impedance verification route (which would need the PCB design files — consistent with publishing Gerbers), not as the basis for photos/X-ray/weight.
5) CYPHEROCK CONFIRMED AND EXTENDABLE. Keylabs public response (cypherock.com/keylabs.pdf, Q3 2022, X1 Wallet): Finding 1 'Test points easily accessible' — 'such test points can be utilized to build a programming jig that can quickly and easily interface with the device as part of a physical evil maid attack and/or as part of a supply chain attack'; Finding 6 'Device Lacks Tamper-Evidence, Tamper-Resistance and Tamper Circuitry' — Cypherock: 'The X1 Wallet is externally powered, meaning any tamper circuitry can be easily spoofed ... the enclosure is ultrasonically welded ... once opened leave visible marks'; Finding 5 (no potting): Cypherock 'will use potting material on MCU and the ATECC' plus conformal coating. The externally-powered argument applies to pq1 too (docs/hardware/hardware_requirements.md:147 — no battery), which is the correct reason IMP-01 is passive/mechanical rather than Foundation-style active tamper.
6) FOUNDATION: cite the audit response, not the glossary. docs.foundation.xyz/glossary/home/ only says 'active tamper detection that monitors whether the device has been physically opened or modified ... erases all sensitive data'. The precise claim is in foundation.xyz/security/passport-prime-audit-response-2025.pdf (Keylabs, Oct 2025): 'JTAG/SWD debug signals ... and test pads connected to the communication of the ATECC608C ... All of these interfaces are covered by the device's display, which itself is protected by tamper detection pins that would trigger security responses upon disassembly attempts'; 'Two active tamper pins with normally-open switches detect device opening from either side and trigger immediate SECURAM clearing'; 'The tamper system would trigger if you removed the screen, and drilling through the screen would leave obvious damage'. Note this is ACTIVE (battery-backed) tamper, a different mechanism from IMP-01's passive destructive-open shell.
7) COLDCARD: vendor pages (coldcard.com/docs/physical-notes, coinkite blog) describe a welded clear polycarbonate case for visual implant/interposer inspection plus a numbered tamper-evident bag whose number the device shows on first boot — confirmed in search snippets only, not fetched.
8) REPO CLAIM 'pq1 has nothing on this axis yet' is slightly overstated: docs/hardware/hardware_requirements.md:108 already lists a 'Case / enclosure switch wired to a TAMP_INx pin' and :242 an 'EMI shielding can over U585 + both SEs ... board not started'; secure/src/hw/tamp.rs + the `tamp`/`tamp-wipe` features exist. These are checklist/firmware-side items, not an enclosure/PCB spec, so the gap stands, but the IMP should say 'no mechanical spec, BOM, or ODM commitment' rather than 'nothing'. docs/hardware/pcb/README.md was not re-read in this pass.
